items.prompt: What kind of animal is the African wild dog?

options.label: A wild canine
options.feedback: Correct — the African wild dog is a wild canine, a member of the dog family that lives in the wild.

options.label: A large cat
options.feedback: Not quite — it belongs to the dog family, not the cat family. Cats are a different group of carnivores.

options.label: A type of hyena
options.feedback: No — although it was once mistakenly named Hyaena picta, it is actually a canid, not a hyena.

options.label: A kind of fox
options.feedback: No — it is a canine, but it is not a fox. Foxes are a different group of wild dogs.

items.ok_line: The African wild dog is a wild canine.
items.ko_line: It is a member of the dog family.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog is a wild canine, which means it belongs to the dog family. Although its scientific name once included 'Hyaena,' it is not a hyena at all — it is a true canid.

items.prompt: Where in the world does the African wild dog live?

options.label: In the forests of South America
options.feedback: No — the African wild dog is native to Africa, not South America. South America has its own wild canids, like the bush dog.

options.label: Across Europe and Asia
options.feedback: Not right — it is found in Africa, not in Europe or Asia. Those continents have other canids, such as wolves and dholes.

options.label: In sub-Saharan Africa
options.feedback: Correct — the African wild dog is native to sub-Saharan Africa, which is the part of Africa south of the Sahara Desert.

options.label: In the deserts of North Africa
options.feedback: No — it lives south of the Sahara, not in the northern deserts. North Africa has a different climate and different wildlife.

items.ko_line: Its home is Africa, south of the Sahara.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog is native to sub-Saharan Africa. This is the large region of Africa that lies south of the Sahara Desert, where the climate and habitats suit this hunting canine.

items.prompt: What does the African wild dog use to catch its prey?

options.label: Ambush from hiding
options.feedback: No — it does not hide and wait like some hunters. It actively pursues its prey over long distances instead.

options.label: Stamina and cooperative hunting
options.feedback: Correct — it uses endurance to run prey down and works together with other pack members to exhaust the animal.

options.label: A venomous bite
options.feedback: No — it has no venom. Its hunting relies on running and teamwork, not poison.

options.label: Sharp claws to climb trees
options.feedback: Not right — it hunts on the ground and does not climb trees to catch prey. Climbing is not part of its hunting method.

items.ok_line: It outlasts prey and hunts together.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog captures its prey by using stamina and cooperative hunting. Rather than a quick ambush, it runs its prey down over time, with pack members working together to tire the animal out.

items.prompt: At what times of day does the African wild dog usually hunt?

options.label: Only at night
options.feedback: No — it does not hunt only in the dark. It is active at dawn and dusk, and sometimes during the day.

options.label: Only in the middle of the day
options.feedback: Not right — while it can be active during the day, its main hunting times are at dawn and dusk.

options.label: Only in the early morning
options.feedback: Partly wrong — dawn is one time it hunts, but it also hunts at dusk, so morning is not the only time.

options.label: At dawn and dusk
options.feedback: Correct — the African wild dog mostly hunts at dawn and dusk, though it can also be active during the day.

items.ok_line: It hunts mostly at dawn and dusk.
items.ko_line: It is active at daybreak and evening.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog is a specialized hunter that mostly hunts at dawn and dusk. It also shows some activity during the day, but those two twilight periods are its main hunting times.

items.prompt: How does the African wild dog feed its young?

options.label: It regurgitates food for them
options.feedback: Correct — like other canids, the African wild dog brings up food from its stomach to feed its pups.

options.label: It lets the pups hunt for themselves immediately
options.feedback: No — the pups are too young to hunt. The adults provide food by regurgitating it for them.

options.label: It carries food back in its paws
options.feedback: Not right — canids do not carry food in their paws. The African wild dog uses its mouth and stomach to bring food to the young.

options.label: It nurses them on milk their whole lives
options.feedback: No — like all mammals, the pups drink milk when very young, but once they are weaned, the adults feed them with regurgitated food.

items.ok_line: Adults bring up food for pups.
items.ko_line: Pups depend on adult food at first.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog regurgitates food for its young, which is a common behavior among canids. This lets the pups eat solid food before they are able to hunt on their own.

items.prompt: What makes the African wild dog's teeth special among canids?

options.label: They are flat for grinding plants
options.feedback: No — the African wild dog is a meat-eater, not a plant-eater. Its teeth are shaped for slicing flesh, not grinding.

options.label: They are specialized for a meat-only diet
options.feedback: Correct — its teeth are highly specialized for hypercarnivory, meaning it eats almost nothing but meat.

options.label: They grow back continuously
options.feedback: Not right — its teeth do not regrow like a rodent's incisors. They are fixed and specialized for cutting meat.

options.label: They are all the same shape
options.feedback: No — like other carnivores, it has different tooth shapes. Its premolars are unusually large, and its carnassials are blade-like.

items.ok_line: Its teeth are built for eating meat.
items.ko_line: They are for slicing flesh, not plants.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog has teeth highly specialized for a hypercarnivorous diet, meaning its diet is almost entirely meat. Its premolars are the largest relative to body size of any living carnivore except the spotted hyena, and its lower carnassials have a blade-like heel for shearing flesh.

items.prompt: What body feature does the African wild dog lack on its forefeet?

options.label: Toes
options.feedback: No — it has toes. It is missing a specific digit, the first one, not all of its toes.

options.label: Claws
options.feedback: Not right — it has claws. The feature it lacks is the dewclaw, which is the first digit on the forefoot.

options.label: Pads
options.feedback: No — it has pads on its feet. What it lacks is the dewclaw, not the pads.

options.label: Dewclaws
options.feedback: Correct — the African wild dog has no dewclaws on its forefeet, and this loss helps increase its stride and speed.

items.ok_line: It lacks dewclaws on its forefeet.
items.ko_line: It has claws, but no dewclaws.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog lacks dewclaws, which are the first digits on the forefeet. This loss increases its stride and speed, helping it pursue prey across open terrain for long distances.

items.prompt: What is the African wild dog's coat known for?

options.label: Having varied colours and patterns
options.feedback: Correct — the African wild dog exhibits some of the most varied coat colours among mammals, with individuals differing greatly.

options.label: Being a single solid colour
options.feedback: No — its coat is not solid. It is a mix of colours and patterns, which is why it is sometimes called the painted dog.

options.label: Changing colour like a chameleon
options.feedback: Not right — its coat does not change colour. The variation is between individuals, not within one dog over time.

options.label: Having stripes like a tiger
options.feedback: No — although it is multicoloured, its patterns are not tiger stripes. The name 'painted' comes from its mottled, blotchy coat.

items.ok_line: Its coat comes in many patterns and colours.
items.ko_line: Its coat varies between individuals, not within one.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog exhibits some of the most varied coat colours among mammals. Individuals differ in patterns and colours, which may serve purposes like communication, concealment, or temperature regulation.

items.prompt: Which of these is another name for the African wild dog?

options.label: Spotted hyena
options.feedback: No — the spotted hyena is a different animal and a competitor, not another name for the African wild dog.

options.label: Cape leopard
options.feedback: Not right — the Cape hunting dog is a name for the African wild dog, not the Cape leopard. A leopard is a cat.

options.label: Painted dog
options.feedback: Correct — the African wild dog is also called the painted dog, a name that suits its multicoloured coat.

options.label: African lion dog
options.feedback: No — that is not a real name for this animal. It is called painted dog, painted wolf, or Cape hunting dog, among others.

items.ok_line: It is also called the painted dog.
items.ko_line: Its other names are painted and hunting dog.
items.exp_text: The African wild dog has several English names, including painted dog, painted wolf, Cape hunting dog, and painted lycaon. The name 'painted dog' is promoted because it helps counteract negative perceptions of the species.
